audit_scope.description: This batch covers: Cancun LOG opcodes, hard fork meta-EIP process (EIP-233), Merkle proof RPC method (EIP-1186), Prague RIPEMD-160 precompile, and Prague block structure including withdrawals and protocol requests.

misclassified_entities.reason: From EIP-233: 'All Core Devs' is a governance body managing hard fork coordination. They do not represent a runtime external entity interacting with the EL protocol.
From EIP-233: 'EIP Authors' proposing EIPs for hard fork inclusion are governance participants, not runtime external entities.
From EIP-233: 'Client Implementation Teams' are developers building EL clients. They do not represent a runtime entity crossing a trust boundary.
From Prague RIPEMD-160: 'Calling Contract' invoking the precompile is internal EVM execution via CALL opcode. The real external entity is whoever submits the transaction.

From Prague RIPEMD-160: 'Untrusted Data Source' described as 'any contract or EOA providing data to be hashed' conflates internal EVM data flow with external trust boundaries. Data reaching the precompile has already entered the system via a transaction.

From Prague blocks: 'System Contracts' that generate protocol requests during execution are internal protocol-level contracts deployed at known addresses. They are part of the EL, not external entities.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client (eth_getProof)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-1186: external clients request Merkle proofs via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. Clients may request proofs for arbitrary addresses and storage keys. The RPC endpoint must handle potentially abusive request patterns (large storage key lists, rapid requests).

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted RPC Provider (Proof Source)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From EIP-1186: when a light client or off-chain verifier receives proofs from an RPC provider, the provider is untrusted. Proof data must be cryptographically verified against a trusted block header (state root). Fabricated proofs must be detectable.

trusted_external_entities.name: CL via Engine API (Beacon Chain Withdrawals)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From Prague blocks: the Beacon Chain consensus layer provides withdrawal requests and block production instructions via the authenticated Engine API (JWT). The channel is authenticated but withdrawal data content must still be validated for format correctness and processed according to protocol rules.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via devp2p (Prague Blocks)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From Prague blocks: peers propagate blocks containing new Prague fields (requests_hash, withdrawal data, multiple transaction types). All block content received over unauthenticated P2P must be fully validated including new Prague-specific fields.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Validator) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: From Prague blocks: validators produce blocks with Prague structure. Block headers are received over unauthenticated P2P and all fields (including requests_hash, withdrawals_root) must be independently recomputed and validated.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: eth_getProof JSON-RPC -> State Trie Lookup -> Merkle Proof Construction
boundary_edges.security_assumption: RPC endpoint must handle arbitrary address and storage key requests without excessive resource consumption. Response must contain valid account proof and storage proofs that can be verified against the state root. Rate limiting should be applied to prevent DoS.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: JSON-RPC response -> Off-chain Proof Verification -> State Root Check
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Proof verifiers must have a trusted block header (from CL or light client sync). All proof nodes must be validated against the state root. Missing or extra proof nodes must cause verification failure. The RPC provider cannot forge a valid proof without knowing the pre-image.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Engine API (engine_newPayload) -> Withdrawal Processing -> State Transition
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Engine API channel is authenticated via JWT. Withdrawal data format must still be validated (valid addresses, amounts). Withdrawals are processed in order and credited to specified addresses. The EL trusts the CL for withdrawal ordering but validates structural correctness.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: devp2p block import -> Full Prague Block Validation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All Prague block fields must be validated: requests_hash must match independently computed value from system contract outputs, withdrawals_root must match withdrawal list, transaction receipts must handle all supported types (including EIP-7702). Ommers must be empty tuple.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P block propagation -> Header + Body Validation
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Validator-produced blocks are untrusted over P2P. All header fields including Prague-specific ones must be independently recomputed. Block body must be consistent with header commitments.
